discoveries: (a) The CLI's stream-json `init` event shows what a session loaded: its connectors, agents, skills, plugins, memory path and tools. (b) `--agent <role>` replaces the default prompt and cuts the tools to the agent's list, so the design appends the role file instead. (c) A resume with `--session-id` needs `--fork-session`, and a resumed session keeps its original's system prompt. (d) `--setting-sources project,local` also drops the owner's user-level ask rules; this was fixed by carrying only the `ask` and `deny` rules. (e) A worktree session's local settings and its fallback skills come from the main checkout. (f) `gov retrieve` handed the test designer passages of this ticket's design note, which DEC-820 (c) says it may not read. (g) The main checkout's local settings `env` (including `GOV_DEV_TIERS`) reaches every worktree worker through the CLI itself (this is W2-56's area).
risks: Every real launch is refused until W2-11 writes the default and version lines (fail closed by design). After the merge, a session started before this change can no longer be resumed through `gov launch`; it must be started fresh. Until W2-56 merges, a parent's `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` still reaches the session's process.
lessons: (1) Run the wait for the gates as a job of its own: my first full run was killed at 94% by the two-hour limit, because waiting for the load and the lock counted against it. (2) Take the verification lock with a holder job (`hold_lock.sh`) and then start the run separately. (3) `rm` in a lead command is refused by the owner's user-level ask rule. (4) A sandboxed worker cannot run live CLI measurements; the lead has to.
